newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - Chinese "window" companies seen in demand.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Chinese "window" companies seen in demand.

text.p: The Hong Kong market's keen interest in red chips is forecast to continue in the months ahead, spurred on by planned initial public offerings (IPOs) of so-called Chinese "window" companies, analysts said.

"Experience tells them (investors) that they can expect a handsome return in an easy and comfortable way, and that underpins demand for these IPOs," said Frankie Szeto, analyst at Tai Fook Securities said.
Red chips are companies listed and based in Hong Kong but operating in China.

Window companies, a newly named category of red chips, are companies established in Hong Kong by Chinese authorities such as municipal and provincial governments, or economic entities supervised by the State Council or ministries.
The same theme that has fueled interest in other red chips -- anticipation of future injections of low priced, mainland-based assets -- is expected to attract investors to these new listings.
"Anticipation of a repetition of the Shanghai Industrial story will make the upcoming IPOs a hot buy and the main market focus," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.

Shares of Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, the Shanghai municipal government's investment arm, have climbed about 507 percent since their listing on May 30, 1996. Debuting last year at HK$7.28, they closed on Friday at HK$44.20.

Beijing Enterprise Ltd, a company based in Hong Kong but backed by the Beijing municipal government, is seen to be one of the most attractive investment opportunities among the impending IPOs, analysts said.

Beijing Enterprise is expected to be brought to the market in May and raise more than HK$1.2 billion with an issue of about 150 million shares at a price of HK$8.00 to HK$9.70 a share. This would give it a price-to-earnings multiple of between 12.7 and 14.8 times.

Despite a relatively high P/E compared with ratios of between six and seven times for other recent IPOs, analysts said they expected Beijing Enterprise to receive an enthusiastic response because of the possibility of future asset injections.
Beijing Enterprise is a diversified mini-conglomerate involved in manufacturing, retailing, road operations, telecommunications and property investment.
Analysts say the offer could get a market reception as strong as that of Shanghai Industrial.
Tianjin Industrial Ltd, backed by the Tianjin municipal government, and Chukong Shipping Ltd, a shipping unit of the Zhuhai municipal government, are also expected to be listed in May or June.
Further down the listing calendar are companies established by the governments of Henan, Hunan, Hebei and Shaanxi provinces.
The Wuhan municipal government is also expected to list its Hong Kong window company later in the year.

"There is a lot of liquidity in the market," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas. "IPOs of these window companies are still seen in hot demand given that the anticipation (of assets injection) is still there."
But analysts also cautioned that investors would become more selective as the supply of red chip shares increased.
